claims.text: The agency has a founding instrument and a first Director, and this node has carried neither. DoD Directive 5105.15 of 7 February 1958, reproduced in full in the agency's own commissioned history, reads: 'In accordance with the provisions of the National Security Act of 1947, as amended, and Reorganization Plan No. 6 of 1953, there is established in the Office of the Secretary of Defense the Department of Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency.' Its mandate is open-ended by design: the Agency is responsible for 'the direction or performance of such advanced projects in the field of research and development as the Secretary of Defense shall, from time to time, designate by individual project or by category', and 'The Director of Advanced Research Projects shall report to the Secretary of Defense.'

desc: DARPA describes itself as 'an independent research and development agency within the U.S. Department of War' and states it was 'Created in response to the launch of Sputnik in 1957' as 'our nation's commitment to never again face a strategic technical surprise'. It runs six technical offices, and its published budget figures as of 2026 are a President's FY2027 request of $5.039 billion against an FY2026 enacted level of $4.322 billion. DARPA's relevance to this board is twofold and mostly negative-space. First, it is named among the contributing elements to ODNI's June 2021 Preliminary Assessment on UAP - the only pure R&D organisation on that list, which implies it was consulted on the 'USG or U.S. industry developmental programs' explanatory category, the category that exists to reconcile UAP reports against black aerospace projects. Second, DARPA is the institutional counterfactual against which the legacy program allegation is measured: DARPA is what an American breakthrough-technology effort looks like when it is run in the open, with named program managers on fixed terms, published solicitations and a public budget. Any organisation performing eighty years of exotic materials exploitation without producing a single DARPA-style transition to a fielded system is either failing or is structured to avoid exactly that visibility.

dossier.narrative: The comparison only works if the agency's own paper is on the board, and now it is. The founding instrument is reproduced in full inside the agency's own commissioned history, and two things in it matter. The establishment clause puts ARPA inside the Office of the Secretary of Defense rather than inside a service, and the mandate is written open-ended by design: the Agency is responsible for such advanced projects in the field of research and development as the Secretary of Defense shall from time to time designate, by individual project or by category. That is a charter that can absorb anything the Secretary points at, which is exactly the shape the legacy allegation describes, and it was published. The second correction is to the officer. The CIA's own chronology, an independent record, states that on 7 February 1958 ARPA was established in DoD with Roy W. Johnson of General Electric named director; Herbert York was the first Chief Scientist and was later elevated to first Director of Defense Research and Engineering. The podcast corpus reverses those two, and no York node is built: the correction belongs here, on the agency.
openQuestions: The issuing office's own copy of DoD Directive 5105.15 was not opened; esd.whs.mil returned HTTP 403 on every path tried, and the directive's text here comes from the ARPA-commissioned history's reproduction of it.
Whether DARPA's role among the contributing elements to ODNI's June 2021 Preliminary Assessment extended beyond the developmental-programs explanatory category.
